page: Microsoft Azure B16ls_v2 is a burstable virtual machine instance within the Bsv2 series, architectured for compute-heavy workloads that feature variable or intermittent CPU demand. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 16 burstable vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The underlying processor features 48 MB of L3 cache alongside support for vector instructions including AVX-512 with VNNI and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES and SHA-NI.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. It operates without bundled local storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on remote premium storage attachments for disk IOPS and throughput. Hyper-V handles virtualization overhead, while memory throughput metrics reflect an uncached large-block read speed of 99.55 GB/sec and a write speed of 56.79 GB/sec.

Benchmark evaluations position the B16ls_v2 consistently within the median tier of multi-core general-purpose cloud servers. The platform achieves a Geekbench 6 multi-core score of 9,950 and a PassMark CPU score of 21,273.81. In task-specific evaluations, the machine delivered 15.93 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, compiled code via Clang with a score of 15,309, and handled static web serving throughput at 21.38 GB/sec. Lightweight AI workloads show prompt processing throughput of 35.07 tokens per second on 7B models.

From an efficiency perspective, the B16ls_v2 offers high vCPU density at a lower qualitative expenditure tier compared to fixed-allocation compute instances. The primary operational tradeoff involves the burstable CPU credit model, which can restrict sustained high-intensity computation when burst credits expire, alongside the total absence of ephemeral local scratch disks. The instance is suited for batch processing, build servers, continuous integration pipelines, and web servers with fluctuating traffic patterns.

The instance lacks local ephemeral storage, directing disk operations to remote storage volumes, and includes no GPU hardware. Benchmark results place it firmly in the middle 50 percent of cloud compute profiles, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 21,273.81 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,950. With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and burstable processor allocation, the B16ls_v2 serves as an economical infrastructure platform for build agents, intermittent microservices, dev-test environments, and web applications that experience periodic spikes in traffic.
